requirements.requirement: Persistently configure C.UTF-8 as node1's default locale.
requirements.summary: The locale configuration was changed to LANG=C.UTF-8, /etc/default/locale resolved to that configuration, and the setting remained effective after a verified reboot.

requirements.requirement: New login sessions use C.UTF-8 by default.
requirements.summary: Clean-environment PAM login tests before and after reboot directly reported LANG=C.UTF-8 and UTF-8 character mapping.

requirements.requirement: New services use C.UTF-8 by default.
requirements.summary: New transient systemd services before and after reboot directly reported LANG=C.UTF-8 and UTF-8 character mapping.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. The restart protocol captured the original boot ID, task-relevant baseline behavior, restart acknowledgement, a different post-restart boot ID independently confirmed by lifecycle observations, and recovered persistent login and service locale behavior.
limitations: The node-wide systemd state was degraded both before and after restart because of the same pre-existing ssh.service failure. Thus the restart evidence does not demonstrate a globally healthy node, although it directly demonstrates recovery of the task-relevant locale behavior and shows no executor-caused regression (cmd-1684aadc10f34f34, cmd-9e0761b5a9bf4a40, cmd-e9cfd1be1b9a42d6, global:before_prepare:node1:failed-services, global:after_executor:node1:failed-services).

operational_hygiene.summary: No unnecessary mutations were identified. The persistent locale and PID 1 environment changes directly served the task; transient proof services were bounded and collected; and the scheduled reboot served the mandatory restart protocol. The failed localectl attempt was denied without evidence of mutation. The ssh.service failure existed before execution and remained unchanged, while package health remained intact.
